facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is classified as a shastasaurid, extending the known range of this family to the latest Triassic.
facts.quote: It is believed to be a shastasaurid, extending the family's range by years up to the latest Triassic.

facts.statement: The genus Ichthyotitan contains only one known species, I. severnensis.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, I. severnensis.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is known from two fragmentary lower jaw bones discovered in 2016 and 2020.
facts.quote: It is known from two fragmentary surangular bones of the lower jaw, discovered in separate places in 2016 and 2020.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ichthyotitan was found near Blue Anchor in Somerset within the Westbury Formation.
facts.quote: The Ichthyotitan holotype specimen, BRSMG Cg3178 (the "BAS specimen"), was discovered in sediments of the Westbury Formation near Blue Anchor in Somerset.

facts.statement: The first fragment of the holotype was discovered on May 28, 2020, by 11-year-old Ruby Reynolds and her father Justin Reynolds.
facts.quote: The first fragment was found on 28 May 2020 by 11-year-old Ruby Reynolds, while looking for fossils on the beach at Blue Anchor with her father, fossil collector Justin Reynolds.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan severnensis was formally described as a new genus and species in 2024 by Lomax et al.
facts.quote: In 2024, Lomax et al. described Ichthyotitan severnensis as a new genus and species of probable shastasaurid ichthyosaur based on BRSMG Cg3178 and BRSMG Cg2488.

facts.statement: The name Ichthyotitan combines the Greek word for fish with a suffix meaning giant.
facts.quote: The generic name, Ichthyotitan, combines a reference to ichthyosaurs—meaning "fish lizard", derived from the Greek word ἰχθύς (ikhthús), meaning "fish"—with the Greek suffix -τιτάν (-titan), meaning "giant".

facts.statement: The species name severnensis refers to the nearby Severn Estuary.
facts.quote: The specific name, severnensis, references the Severn Estuary near the type locality.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is estimated to have reached nearly 25 meters in length, making it the largest known marine reptile.
facts.quote: Estimates scaling up the bones from other ichthyosaur species put Ichthyotitan body length at nearly 25 m, which would make it the largest marine reptile currently known.

facts.statement: Revised anatomical comparisons suggest Ichthyotitan was 25 meters long, likely the largest marine reptile ever described.
facts.quote: Comparing the position of the MAME process in the BAS specimen to that in Besanosaurus, they provided a revised length estimate of 25 m, likely making it the largest marine reptile ever described.

facts.statement: Tentatively linked Aust specimens are informally estimated to be even larger, reaching 30 to 35 meters in length.
facts.quote: The Aust specimens, tentatively linked to Ichthyotitan, have been informally estimated to be even larger at 30 to 35 m long.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is the only known shastasaurid from the Rhaetian, appearing 13 million years after its relatives.
facts.quote: Ichthyotitan is the only shastasaurid and giant ichthyosaur to be known from the Rhaetian, found in the fossil record 13 million years after their relatives.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan exhibits a unique condition among ichthyosaurs where the surangular and angular bones may have been fused in life.
facts.quote: Along with the continuous bone structure, this implies that the bones were possibly fused in life, a unique condition among ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan was likely an active predator that hunted smaller prey, including other marine reptiles, in an orca-like manner.
facts.quote: Ichthyotitan is believed to have been a predator, hunting smaller prey including other marine reptiles in a fashion similar to an orca.

facts.statement: Evidence of scavenging on Ichthyotitan fossils before burial explains the scarcity of known remains.
facts.quote: Their ecology made their remains vulnerable to scavengers, with one of the fossils showing signs of scavenging before burial, explaining the scarcity of known fossils.

facts.statement: The unique morphology of the posterior jaw in the Cuers specimen has been debated but is now linked to Ichthyotitan.
facts.quote: The morphology of the posterior jaw was considered unique at the time of discovery, but has since been linked to Ichthyotitan specimens.

facts.statement: It is debated whether shastasaurids were suction-feeders, as current research suggests their jaw structure does not fit that profile.
facts.quote: Older studies have suggested that shastasaurids were suction-feeders, but current research indicates that the jaws of shastasaurid ichthyosaurs do not fit the suction-feeding profile.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is known from two suprangular bones, which are parts of the jaw.
facts.quote: Es conocido por dos huesos suprangulares (parte de la mandíbula).

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is estimated to have reached a body length of nearly 25 meters, potentially making it the largest known marine reptile.
facts.quote: Pudo haber tenido una longitud corporal cercana a los 25 metros, lo que lo convertiría en el reptil marino más grande conocido a la fecha.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 205 to 202 million years ago, in Somerset, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: de la formación Westbury Mudstone, del Triásico Superior, hace aproximadamente entre 205 a 202 millones de años (Rhaetiense tardío), de Somerset, Reino Unido.

facts.statement: The first specimen of Ichthyotitan, known as the Lilstock specimen (BRSMG Cg2488), was discovered in 2016.
facts.quote: El primer espécimen que luego se conocería como Ichthyotitan, BRSMG Cg2488 (el "espécimen de Lilstock"), se encontró en 2016.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen (BRSMG Cg3178) was found in sediments of the Westbury Formation near Blue Anchor, Somerset, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, BRSMG Cg3178, fue descubierto entre los sedimentos de la formación Westbury cerca de Blue Anchor en Somerset, Reino Unido.

facts.statement: The first fragment of the holotype was found in 2020, with further expeditions until 2022 revealing additional pieces.
facts.quote: El primer fragmento se encontró en 2020, y expediciones posteriores hasta 2022 revelaron más piezas.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan severnensis was formally described as a new genus and species of probable shastasaurid ichthyosaur by Lomax et al. in 2024.
facts.quote: En 2024, Lomax et al. describieron a Ichthyotitan severnensis como un nuevo género y especie de un probable ictiosaurio shastasáurido basado en BRSMG Cg3178 y BRSMG Cg2488.

facts.statement: The genus name Ichthyotitan combines the name Ichthyosaurus, meaning 'fish lizard', with the Greek suffix '-titan', meaning 'giant'.
facts.quote: El nombre del género, Ichthyotitan, combina una referencia a Ichthyosaurus —cuyo nombre significa "pez lagarto", combinando las palabras griegas "ichthys", que significa "pez", y "sauros", que significa "lagarto", con el sufijo griego "-titan", que significa "gigante".

facts.statement: The specific name severnensis refers to the Severn estuary near the type locality.
facts.quote: El nombre específico, severnensis, hace referencia al estuario del río Severn cerca de la localidad tipo.

facts.statement: Histological characteristics suggest the holotype specimen was still growing, indicating it was a subadult or young adult.
facts.quote: sus características histológicas sugieren que el espécimen todavía estaba creciendo, por lo que era un subadulto o un adulto joven.

facts.statement: Using Shastasaurus sikanniensis as a model, researchers estimated Ichthyotitan to be nearly the size of a blue whale.
facts.quote: Utilizando a Shastasaurus sikanniensis como modelo, los investigadores estimaron que el ictiosaurio medía alrededor de de largo, casi el tamaño de una ballena azul.

facts.statement: Scaling based on Besanosaurus yielded a shorter length estimate of 22 meters.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la escala basada en Besanosaurus encontró una estimación de longitud más corta, de 22 metros.

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is classified as a probable shastasaurid ichthyosaur.
facts.quote: un probable shastasáurido ictiosaurio

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan belongs to the parent group Shastasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Shastasauridae

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is assigned to the family Shastasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Shastasauridae

facts.statement: Ichthyotitan is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The time range for Ichthyotitan is the Rhaetian stage, from 205.7 to 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)
